newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CESARE MALDINI LANDS JOB AS COACH OF ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CESARE MALDINI LANDS JOB AS COACH OF ITALY.

text.p: Cesare Maldini, Italy's popular under-21 soccer coach and a former Italian international, was named on Sunday as new coach of the national team.
The widely expected appointment was the first act of new soccer federation president, Luciano Nizzola, who vowed after his election on Saturday to solve Italy's soccer problems.
Maldini, 64, replaces Arrigo Sacchi who resigned two weeks ago to return to coaching his old club AC Milan.
"Cesare Maldini is the new coach of the national team," Nizzola said in statement, adding that Maldini would be officially presented at a news conference at Rome's Olympic Stadium on Monday.

Maldini will make his debut on the bench when Italy play England next February in a crucial World Cup qualifier at Wembley -- the ground where he lifted the European Cup as captain of AC Milan in 1963.
The new coach inherits a national team still recovering form and morale after last June's humiliating first round elimination from the European championship.
Since then, Italy have enjoyed two unconvincing wins over Moldova and Georgia in their opening World Cup qualifiers, followed by an embarrassing defeat to Bosnia in a friendly in Sarajevo last month.
The national side's dismal performances and mounting pressure for the removal of the unpopular Sacchi has also contributed to falling attendances at Italy's home matches.

By winning three successive European Under-21 championships, Maldini has enjoyed the kind of success that Sacchi had promised to deliver on his appointment in 1991, and he was a natural candidate to take Sacchi's place.
Maldini also served as assistant to Enzo Bearzot when Italy last won the World Cup in 1982.
Significantly, almost all the players in the current Italian team, captained by Maldini's son Paolo, have emerged from his under-21 ranks.
Unlike Sacchi, who never played professionally, Maldini won four league titles as a Milan player in the 1950s and 60s as well as the 1963 European Cup, when Milan beat Portugal's Benfica 2-1.
Sacchi was asked to comment on Maldini's widely-expected appointment as coach just minutes before the announcement was made.
"Lots of luck to my great friend Cesare," Sacchi said. "I wish him every success."
Maldini's appointment, just 24-hours after Nizzola's appointment as soccer federation president, heralds a new era for Italian soccer.
"We are here to show that soccer is united again," Nizzola said on Saturday. "We are here to give soccer a stable government to solve its problems."
